newsitem.title: UK: Man shot dead by "IRA front group" in N.Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Man shot dead by "IRA front group" in N.Ireland.

text.p: An organisation which police say is a front for IRA guerrillas claimed responsibility for shooting dead a 30-year-old man on Monday, its latest victim in a self-styled purge of alleged drug-dealers.
Using a recognised codeword, a caller for the so-called "Direct Action Against Drugs" (DAAD) told a Belfast radio station that its men had carried out the killing in a Catholic district.

British security sources believe that seven men shot dead last year were victims of DAAD, whose supporters branded them drug-dealers. Police officers say DAAD is a cover name used by Irish Republican Army guerrillas.
Police said two gunmen burst into a house and shot the man three times in the head before escaping. A 12-year-old girl was in the house but was not hurt.
DAAD said the man had been heavily involved in drug-dealing. Local residents said the IRA had ordered him to stay out of the area last year.
Last year police and politicians said the killers were in reality IRA guerrillas intent on bringing gunlaw back to streets which had been a guerrilla war zone for 25 years.
Police chiefs said IRA hardliners were aiming to tighten control of areas where pro-Irish Catholics regard the mainly Protestant pro-British police with suspicion.
The group's last suspected killing was last January.

The IRA has carried out a string of bombings in mainland Britain and one attack on a British army base in Germany since February but has not launched attacks against British forces in Northern Ireland in its renewed hostilities against rule from London.

Irish media reported on Monday that the guerrillas are considering holding a secret conference to agree a new truce to pave the way for full-scale peace talks on Northern Ireland. But the IRA's Sinn Fein political wing has ruled out an early ceasefire.
